rules.title: The remote branch moved ahead
rules.summary: Git rejected the push because it would discard commits already on the remote branch.

any: Updates were rejected because the remote contains work

causes: Someone else pushed to the branch.
The local branch was rewritten or created from an older base.
actions: Fetch the remote and inspect the commits you are missing.
Merge or rebase intentionally, resolve conflicts, then push again.
Force-push only when the branch policy and collaborators explicitly allow history replacement.

rules.title: Git needs merge conflicts resolved
rules.summary: Both histories changed overlapping content and Git cannot choose a result.

any: you need to resolve your current index first

causes: Two branches changed the same lines or file operation.
A previous merge or rebase is still in progress.
actions: Run git status to list every conflicted path.
Resolve each path based on intended behavior, then test before continuing.
Abort the merge or rebase if it was started by mistake.

rules.title: Git does not trust this repository owner
rules.summary: The repository directory is owned by another account, so Git disabled repository-local configuration.
causes: A container, administrator, sandbox, or different user created the repository.
The directory was copied with ownership metadata.
actions: Verify the repository path and owner before trusting it.
Fix ownership when it is wrong.
Use a narrowly scoped safe.directory entry only when the ownership difference is expected.

rules.title: Git authentication failed
rules.summary: The remote did not accept the supplied SSH key, token, or credential.
causes: The credential is expired, missing, or for a different account.
The account lacks access to the repository.
The remote URL uses a protocol that is not configured.
actions: Confirm the remote URL and intended account.
Re-authenticate through the hosting provider's supported flow.
Verify repository permission without placing tokens in the remote URL.
